name: Vomit
lede: Vomit is a crude name for a sour, olive-leaning yellow-green, in the lists of joke and survey color names rather than any paint, dye or standard.

sections.title: A name with no history
sections.body: The swatch comes from the xkcd color survey, a crowdsourced list of names, and no pigment, dye or dictionary entry of the name is documented in the books [1]. The name is descriptive and rude by design, a way of calling a color unpleasant. Its nearest named neighbor in our library is [[khaki]], at a distance of about 10 CIEDE2000 units, and it sits between [[olive]] and [[chartreuse]] [1].

sections.title: What the books do say
sections.body: The painter and filmmaker Derek Jarman lists *vomit* among the cheap paints he mixed himself in the 1960s, naming it beside "goose turd green" [2]. He also uses it to describe the sickly green of 1950s science fiction, a color of pus and rotting flesh [2]. Elsewhere the word turns up only in the literal sense, as in Finlay's account of poisoning and in descriptions of how shellfish were milked for dye [3][4]. It is not a color name there.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This yellow-green is rare in painting: it fills at least five per cent of the canvas in 12 of 23,781 museum paintings, within six units of CIEDE2000 [5]. The largest share is a Basohli manuscript page of 1760, where it covers about 60 per cent [5]. Seven of the twelve are from the 1900s, a rate more than eight times the archive average [5]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings; a color match is not a pigment test [5].
